title: Security posture discovery with Aether Data
summary: Discovery focused on whether Redwood Hosted can meet Aether Data's compliance needs. Customer prefers hosted for speed but has strict SOC2/ISO requirements, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC and audit logs, KMS/HSM integration, and data residency controls. Discussed Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs: cost and timeline vs compliance and isolation. Agreed next step: send SOC2/ISO artifacts, security whitepaper, and schedule technical deep dive + pilot for workload benchmarking.
next_steps: Alex to send SOC2 report, ISO summary, and security whitepaper (by 2026-03-18)
Samir to schedule technical deep dive / infra workshop with Chris and Priya (propose slots week of 3/23)
Customer to share sample compliance checklist and retention policy (Aether)
Set up 2-week Dedicated pilot quote if needed (Redwood sales)
Follow up meeting to confirm pilot scope and timeline

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-16
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Jordan Lee (Aether CTO), Priya Nair (Aether Head of Security), Chris Huang (Aether Platform Eng), Maya Brooks (Aether Compliance)

Summary notes (auto): quick discovery on security posture, hosted vs dedicated vs private options, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, KMS/encryption, data retention and residency.

00:00 Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm alex from redwood. quick intros?
00:08 Jordan: yeah thanks alex, jordan here, cto at aether. we've been evaluating a couple inference providers for our analytics pipelines, concern is compliance and data residency.
00:18 Priya: hi all, priya, head of security. i have a list of requirements - SOC2, iso27001, sso with our okta, scim, and we need strong audit logging and kms integration.
00:30 Samir: great, i'll try to cover the technical bits — samir, i'm the se. quick question, are you leaning hosted first or thinking dedicated/private out of the gate?
00:40 Jordan: hosted would be fastest but we need to validate compliance; if hosted can't meet our controls we may look at dedicated or private. timeline is tight — want to pilot in april.
00:55 Alex: makes sense, we'll walk through where hosted covers controls and where Dedicated/Private add guarantees like VPC isolation and customer-managed keys.
01:10 Chris: i have a couple infra questions, like how do you handle encryption at rest and key management — do you support customer-managed keys / HSM?
01:20 Samir: yes, for Private deployments we support KMS/HSM integrations and for Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS in many cloud providers; hosted offers encryption-at-rest with our managed keys, but we also have bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options for higher tiers.
01:36 Priya: BYOK for hosted — can you be specific? we need proof we can rotate keys, access control, and audit logs showing key usage.
01:46 Samir: absolutely — we can provide key rotation docs and we emit key-use events to our audit logs; for BYOK the customer controls key lifecycle in their KMS and we request decryption tokens scoped to the workload. i'll attach the BYOK flow in the doc.
02:02 Maya: also data residency — we process PII and some regulated datasets, so we need regional processing and log residency in eu-west.
02:12 Alex: we support region pinning for hosted and Dedicated clusters; Private can be fully on-prem. for hosted we have eu regions and can configure routing policies so requests are served in region.
02:25 Jordan: ok, SOC2 and ISO — do you have reports we can review?
02:30 Alex: yes, SOC2 Type II report and ISO27001 statement. i'll share the artifacts after this call.
02:40 Priya: good, and what about SSO — we use Okta SAML and SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle. need RBAC tied to corporate groups.
02:52 Samir: we support SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC that maps to SAML groups. there are some small differences between hosted and Private: hosted integrates with customer IdP via SAML SSO + SCIM for accounts, Dedicated can be put inside your VPC with direct connectivity and SSO flows use your internal IdP if desired.
03:12 Chris: does RBAC support fine-grained roles? like token-level, route-level access?
03:18 Samir: yes we have role types: admin, devops, dev, read-only, and we can create custom roles for route/model access and token scoping; audit logs capture policy changes.
03:30 Jordan: audit logs — are they immutable? retention? and can we ship logs to our SIEM?
03:38 Samir: logs are append-only in our system; we support log-forwarding to customer SIEMs (S3, Splunk, Datadog) and you can set retention policies. for Dedicated/Private you can choose to keep logs inside your VPC.
03:52 Priya: we need at least 7 years for some records, is that possible?
03:58 Alex: we can support long retention via archive to your storage; hosted default retention is shorter but we can set longer windows as a paid add-on or in Dedicated. we'll need to confirm exact SLAs with legal.
04:15 Jordan: what about data in-flight encryption and network controls — mTLS between clients and API?
04:22 Samir: yes, we enforce TLS 1.2/1.3 for all traffic; Private deployments can be set up with mutual TLS internal to the cluster and we have private endpoints for VPC peering.
04:34 Maya: any pen-testing or third-party audits?
04:38 Alex: we do annual pen tests and vulnerability scans; summary results are in our security pack. we'll share an executive summary and contact info for our security team.
04:50 Chris: curious about model caching and KV cache — does that persist user data anywhere that would be a compliance risk?
04:58 Samir: KV cache is per-session and we can configure TTL and purging policies. by default we don't persist user PII in model cache; for Dedicated/Private customers we can enable stricter in-memory-only policies.
05:12 Priya: ok good. one more — what about data deletion requests and retention policy enforcement?
05:18 Alex: we support data deletion APIs and workflows mapped to retention policies; for hosted we'll perform deletions per SLA, and for Dedicated/Private you can manage deletion directly. we'll document timelines.
05:30 Jordan: cost question — Dedicated seems attractive for compliance, but how long to stand up and what cost premium?
05:38 Alex: Dedicated typically has a provisioning lead time (2-6 weeks depending on capacity and region). cost is higher due to reserved GPU capacity, but you gain performance predictability and data isolation. Private on-prem is longer (months) and involves infra integration.
05:55 Priya: any HIPAA or healthcare controls? we are not healthcare but some partners are — curious if you support BAA.
06:03 Alex: we have customers in regulated spaces; BAA is evaluated case-by-case. we can discuss legal requirements as part of enterprise contracting.
06:12 Jordan: timeline — we want to pilot in april, ideally with hosted but with controls validated. can you provide a pilot quote and what minimal controls we'd need?
06:22 Samir: yes, minimal controls for hosted pilot: SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO + SCIM, audit log export to your SIEM, BYOK for higher tier or Dedicated. we can run a short benchmark to validate latency/costs.
06:38 Maya: do you have any references or customers in finance with similar needs?
06:43 Alex: yes, we can share redacted references; i'll include a short list.
06:48 Jordan: great. next steps?
06:50 Alex: i'll send SOC2/ISO docs and security whitepaper, samir will draft tech deep dive agenda and benchmark plan, and we'll schedule a follow-up week of 3/23. if pilot needs Dedicated we'll produce a quote.
07:05 Priya: sounds good. thanks.
07:08 Alex: thanks everyone.

(Transcript ends — minor transcription errors possible. Speakers occasionally overlap and some proper nouns may be misrecognized.)
